body:
m1 - IMPLEMENTED d_ent AND STOPPED BEFORE UPDATING EXPECTATIONS, because the change has a consequence the ruling did not anticipate and I do not think I should paper over it by re-pinning literals.

WHAT I DID: cost.scala dEnt returns Estimate.missing(AllMissing) on empty specified participants and Estimate.observed(...) otherwise, formula untouched; Entity moved from `always` to `optional`; Entity added to MayBeMissing and NOT to HasReductionReceipt, since like Sensory it has no chart source. Compiles.

RESULT: align 188/192. FOUR FAILURES, AND TWO OF THEM ARE BEHAVIOURAL, NOT PINNED LITERALS:

  WorkedExampleSuite "'Stephen King' goes to the Association external state, not to a source node"
    -> source mass = 0.2562
  WorkedExampleSuite "support density: ... an external unit is light"
  SignatureSuite chronology  0.039516 -> 0.104070   (2.6x)
  SignatureSuite specificity 0.678220 -> 0.659371

THE MECHANISM, and this is the part that differs from d_sens. blend is:

  CostTerm.values.flatMap(t => terms.get(t).map(weights(t) * _)).sum + functionPrior

AN ABSENT TERM CONTRIBUTES NOTHING. So:
  - d_sens imputed 0.0. Its contribution was 0. Making it Missing removed a zero - NO COST CHANGE.
  - d_ent imputed 0.5 at default weight 0.4. Its contribution was 0.2. Making it Missing REMOVES A
    0.2 PENALTY from every cell of every participant-less unit.

So recording absence honestly has ALSO REMOVED A PENALTY, uniformly, for exactly the units the term could not evaluate. Participant-less units are now CHEAPER TO ANCHOR EVERYWHERE, and the Stephen King assertion failing is that showing up behaviourally: a unit that should sit in Association now carries 0.256 source mass.

I DO NOT THINK THAT IS OBVIOUSLY WRONG, and I am not asserting it is a defect. There is a real argument that a term we cannot evaluate should not be charged, and that the old 0.5 was a fabricated penalty. But it is a SECOND EFFECT beyond "record absence", and your requirement 2 was explicitly that we not move two things at once because it confounds the reasons a number changed. This confounds them anyway - not by retuning the formula, but because for a term whose imputed value was NONZERO, recording absence IS a retune.

THREE WAYS FORWARD, and I have not chosen:
  (a) ACCEPT the behaviour. Update the two WorkedExampleSuite expectations, re-pin the two literals,
      re-cut the golden, and state in the commit that removing a fabricated penalty made
      participant-less units more anchorable. Honest, and it moves alignment.
  (b) KEEP THE TOTAL STABLE. Record Entity as missing AND renormalise the blend over present terms
      so absence does not act as a discount. That is a bigger change and touches every term.
  (c) REVERT and leave d_ent imputed, on the grounds that the cure moves alignment more than the
      disease did.

My lean is (a), because (b) changes the semantics of every absent term including the ones you just ruled on, and (c) leaves a known fabricated value in place. But (a) moves published alignment on our only fixture, and after today I am not going to make that call myself.

Nothing is committed. cost.scala and wire.scala are reserved under rv-01M177G58CDSA5B6ZR9G2MBC9D and I will hold them until you rule, or release them if you would rather someone else take it.
